overview.title: 📖 Overview: The First Mishna in Shas
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 2a–2b
overview.hebrewSource: מֵאֵימָתַי קוֹרִין אֶת שְׁמַע בָּעֲרָבִין? מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִים לֶאֱכוֹל בִּתְרוּמָתָן
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The Talmud opens with Shema because reciting it is the daily acceptance of the yoke of Heaven. The mishna asks from when the evening Shema may be said and answers with an unusual sign: the moment priests who were impure may eat their teruma. The Gemara then asks why the mishna assumes we already know there is an obligation, why evening precedes morning, and what exactly that priestly sign means. Along the way it untangles four separate baraitot that each define nightfall differently.

slides.title: ⏰ Until When? Three Opinions in the Mishna
slides.subtitle: The mishna gives one starting point but three end points
rows: 'When you lie down' = the time people go to bed
A rabbinic fence to keep people from delaying
'When you lie down' = the whole time people are asleep

callout.label: Rabban Gamliel's sons:
callout.text: They came home from a wedding after midnight and had not recited Shema. Their father ruled: if dawn has not come, you are still obligated. He explained that even the Rabbis agree by Torah law; 'until midnight' is only a safeguard, just like burning the fats of offerings and eating sacrifices, which are Torah-permitted all night but restricted by the Sages to midnight.

slides.title: 🤔 Why Does the Tanna Start With 'From When'?
slides.subtitle: The Gemara's two opening questions on the very first mishna

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: On what basis does the tanna ask from when? He speaks as if the obligation is already known, but this is the first mishna in all of Shas!

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: And why teach the evening Shema first? Most mitzvot are daytime mitzvot. Teach the morning first!

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: Both questions have one answer. The tanna stands on the verse: בְּשׇׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ, 'when you lie down and when you arise' (Deut. 6:7). The Torah itself states the obligation and puts lying down before rising.

lines.speaker: Alt.
lines.text: If you wish, say instead that he learns it from Creation: וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר, 'there was evening and there was morning, one day'. A day begins at night.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Then why does the later mishna list the morning blessings (two before, one after) before the evening ones (two before, two after)?

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: Having begun with evening and then reached morning, the tanna finished explaining morning while he was on it, and only then returned to the evening blessings.

callout.label: Big idea:
callout.text: The Oral Torah opens by mirroring the order of the Written Torah — evening Shema first.

slides.title: ⭐ Why 'When Priests Eat Teruma' Instead of 'When the Stars Come Out'?
slides.subtitle: The mishna's roundabout sign teaches a second halakha in passing

nodes.content: ❓ Priests eat teruma at the emergence of the stars. Why not just say 'from the emergence of the stars'?
💡 The phrasing teaches something extra: an impure priest who immersed may eat teruma once the stars emerge, even before bringing his atonement offering
📜 Baraita on Leviticus 22:7 — 'And the sun sets and it is purified (וְטָהֵר), and afterward he may eat of the holy things'

columns.label: Reading A
columns.content: The day is purified: sunset is complete, the sky clears, stars emerge. Only nightfall is required.

columns.label: Reading B
columns.content: The person is purified: 'sunset' means the start of sunset, and the priest must also bring his offering.

nodes.content: ✅ Rabba bar Rav Sheila: had the Torah meant the person, it would say 'and he shall be purified' (וְיִטְהַר). 'The day is purified' — as people say, 'the sun has set and the day has cleared'. The Sages of Eretz Yisrael reached the same conclusion from our baraita.

callout.label: Result:
callout.text: Sunset in the verse means complete nightfall, and the atonement offering is not a prerequisite for eating teruma.

slides.title: 🍞 Four Baraitot, Many Signs of Nightfall
slides.subtitle: The Gemara reconciles seemingly contradictory descriptions of when evening Shema begins

boxes.title: Priest's Teruma
items: Our mishna, Rabbi Yehoshua, the Rabbis of the Tosefta
Proof from Nehemiah 4:15–16: work went 'from dawn until the stars came out', and that span is called 'day'

boxes.title: Poor Man's Meal
items: Baraita: 'from when a poor person enters to eat bread with salt'
Conclusion: this is a separate, later time than the priest's — otherwise Rabbi Ḥanina would equal Rabbi Yehoshua

boxes.title: Other Opinions
items: Rabbi Meir (Tosefta): when people eat their Shabbat-eve meal
Rabbi Eliezer: when the day becomes sanctified on Shabbat eve (sunset)
Rabbi Meir (baraita): when priests immerse for teruma
Rabbi Aḥai: when most people recline for a weekday meal

callout.label: Method:
callout.text: Whenever two named opinions would collapse into one, the Gemara concludes they must describe different times. That is how it proves the poor man's time is distinct from, and later than, the priest's.

slides.title: 🌗 Rabbi Yehuda vs. Rabbi Meir: Can Immersion Time Be 'Night'?
slides.subtitle: The dispute turns on how long twilight (bein hashemashot) lasts

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rabbi Meir: evening Shema may begin from when the priests immerse in order to eat teruma
2️⃣ Rabbi Yehuda objects: priests immerse while it is still day. How can that be the time of 'lying down'?
3️⃣ Background: Rabbi Yehuda holds twilight lasts a long while after sunset; Rabbi Yosei holds it is like the blink of an eye just before the stars emerge
4️⃣ Rabbi Meir replies: I am not using your twilight. I follow Rabbi Yosei — priests immerse in that instant before the stars, which already counts as night

callout.label: Takeaway:
callout.text: The halakhic definition of 'night' is not one fixed moment; several tannaitic clocks are running, and the Gemara maps each opinion onto its clock.

summary.principle: The Oral Torah begins where the Written Torah does — 'when you lie down' — and nightfall for Shema is the emergence of the stars, the moment purified priests may eat teruma.

flowSteps.content: 📖 Mishna: evening Shema from when priests eat teruma; until end of first watch / midnight / dawn
❓ Why 'from when'? Why evening first? → Deut. 6:7 'when you lie down…arise'; Genesis 'evening then morning'
⭐ Priests eat teruma at emergence of stars → also teaches: atonement offering not required (Lev. 22:7, 'the day is purified')

columns.content: 🍞 Poor man's meal = a later time than the priest's
🌗 R' Meir's 'immersion' = night per R' Yosei's blink-of-an-eye twilight

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Rabbinic 'until midnight' is a fence; by Torah law the evening Shema and night-mitzvot extend until dawn

quiz.q: According to the mishna, from when may one recite the evening Shema?
o: From sunset on Friday evening
From when the priests enter to eat their teruma
From when a poor person sits down to eat
From midnight
quiz.e: The mishna's sign is the moment purified priests may eat teruma, which the Gemara identifies with the emergence of the stars.

quiz.q: Why does the Gemara say the tanna taught the evening Shema before the morning Shema?
o: Because evening Shema is the more important of the two
Because the Torah writes 'when you lie down' before 'when you arise', and Creation counts evening before morning
Because most mitzvot apply at night
Because the priests eat teruma only at night
quiz.e: The Gemara offers two reasons: the order of Deuteronomy 6:7 ('when you lie down and when you arise') and the order of Creation ('there was evening and there was morning').

quiz.q: What extra halakha does the mishna teach by saying 'when priests eat teruma' rather than 'when the stars emerge'?
o: That teruma may only be eaten at night
That a priest must bring his atonement offering before eating teruma
That failing to bring an atonement offering does not prevent a purified priest from eating teruma
That priests must immerse after the stars emerge
quiz.e: Once the sun has fully set ('the day is purified'), the immersed priest may eat teruma even though his atonement offering has not yet been brought.

quiz.q: What did Rabban Gamliel tell his sons who returned from a wedding after midnight without having recited Shema?
o: They had missed the obligation entirely
They should recite it, but without its blessings
If dawn had not yet arrived, they were still obligated to recite it
They should recite the morning Shema twice
quiz.e: Rabban Gamliel held that Shema may be recited until dawn, and he explained that even the Rabbis' 'until midnight' is only a safeguard against delay.

quiz.q: How does Rabbi Meir answer Rabbi Yehuda's objection that priests immerse while it is still day?
o: He concedes and retracts his opinion
He says he follows Rabbi Yosei, for whom twilight is like the blink of an eye, so the immersion just before the stars is already night
He says priests actually immerse after the stars emerge
He says Shema may be recited during the daytime
quiz.e: Rabbi Meir clarifies that he relies on Rabbi Yosei's definition of bein hashemashot as an instant before the emergence of the stars, so the priests' immersion at that moment is considered night.
